The strongest positive signals are wordless outerwear editorials (Columbia hood-up frost shot, TNFxSKIMS head-to-toe camel): flat sky-white backgrounds, one or two tones, product filling 70% of frame — this maps 1:1 onto identical-geometry color lineups and should become the default hero-slide prompt. Third repeating device: the CapsulesWB артикул-collage grammar (look photo + white-background cutouts + артикул/цена in serif + sparkles) is the proven RU Pinterest→WB traffic format and is trivially automatable from twin cutouts.

The strongest repeating winner is the labeled cutout grid (capsule taxonomy): serif/script header + small-caps labels + neutral-palette cutouts on white — three of the four A-grades share it, and it maps 1:1 onto our identical-geometry twin packshots, so it should become a parameterized template (header style, N cells, RU labels, brand footer). Second pattern: faceless or looking-away street OOTD where a dark puffer is 'de-utilitarianized' by beige accessories (beanie/scarf/knit/gold) — encode this exact styling formula into twin-on-model render prompts, including AI-look city-dusk scenes which demonstrably perform. Third: same-silhouette colorway repetition as a still-life device (stacked/fanned color twins) — our color lineups are born for it on both Pinterest and WB card slides.

The gold in this batch is the capsule architecture: clean cutout grids on one white field with sparse letterspaced labels (497c77, 504ef8) and the items-to-outfits proof ladder (a125fb) — all three are almost mechanically populated by our identical-geometry color-twin cutouts, so encode "grid of twins + row taxonomy + 1 header" as a generation template. Second repeating device: the try-on video cover with a centered two-layer pill title over a headless garment crop (b80afb) — the strongest Wibes first-frame formula here. The O'STIN/Befree catalog half of the batch is mostly off-category filler; the single device worth extracting is Befree's rotated sidebar артикул caption that makes a premium editorial shoppable without breaking it with plates.

The dominant winning grammar in this batch is the premium clean-packshot code: full-body model centered on a white/tinted void, coat worn open or half-zipped over a TONAL base layer (whole outfit sampled from the jacket's hue family), zero text, one prop max — Aritzia/ARKET/COS all monetize minimalism as a price-tier signal, and it maps 1:1 onto NORVIA twin renders. Second repeating device: the franchise matrix — the same puffer shot in identical pose/crop across length and color variants (Super Puff Long/Shorty, ARKET black/green/beige), which is exactly what our identical-geometry color lineups were built for; encode 'same frame, same pose, vary length x color' as a generation rule. Third: trust-framing via commerce metadata (Befree's rotated SKU spine, ARKET's PDP-screenshot pin with visible price, Zara fitting-room selfie) — pins that look findable/buyable beat pins that look like ads, so bake артикул and WB-style UI chrome into Pinterest creatives.

This batch's dominant pattern is "color as the content unit": outfits and catalogs are consistently reduced to labeled color chips — additive formulas (photo + Blue+Orange+White equation), pairwise combination matrices, jacket-to-bottoms chip fans, and Pantone-coded trend grids that borrow professional authority. For NORVIA generation prompts, encode: (1) every twin colorway ships with 2-3 named companion-color chips and a plus-sign formula layout, (2) Pantone-style coded palette bars mapping our lineup to the FW season for authority pins, (3) same-silhouette multi-colorway strips with one deliberate bright accent among neutrals. Secondary winning pattern: tonal head-to-toe styling in snowy Russian-architecture scenes and walking b-roll with hollow outline CTA text — both map one-to-one onto our twin-animation Wibes pipeline.

This batch splits into two production tiers NORVIA can encode immediately. Tier 1 (12 STOREEZ GI Capsule pattern, repeated across 6+ pins): zero on-image text, one tonal color story where garment, styling and location share a temperature, one strong scene anchor (vintage car, diner booth, bookshelf, concrete garage), and crucially face-averted or chin-down crops — which is a gift for AI-twin content because it hides the hardest-to-fake element while foregrounding garment geometry. Tier 2 (ecom pins): the garment alone carries the frame — ghost-mannequin hero + single CTA pill, styled no-model shelf still-life, and 3-colorway collage with keyword headline — all reproducible today from existing twin packshots and color lineups with just an infographic layer. Encode into generation prompts: 'tonal monochrome scene matched to colorway + headless crop' for editorial, and 'centered twin + one pill CTA endcard' for conversion formats.

The dominant reproducible pattern is the product-cutout outfit collage: one outerwear hero at ~2x scale plus 4-7 flat basics on pure white — three of the strongest refs (506ec, a29e1, 79d00) are variations of it, and it maps 1:1 onto our twin packshots for Pinterest and WB card slides. Second pattern: color discipline as the hook — either full ton-sur-ton (garment and environment in one hue family, c1d09) or a single color echo between coat and accessory (15a93); both are one-line additions to twin-scene generation prompts. For GRWM/wibes, the canon is a two-beat structure — garment held up on a hanger center-frame, then a centered two-tier serif-caps + script title naming the exact item — while a third of the 'flat_lay'-labeled refs were actually collages, selfies, or street style, so archetype labels in the source data need re-tagging before prompt encoding.

This batch resolves into three encodable molecules. (1) The dominant video-cover device is a count-promise hook ('N ways to wear...') set as a centered two-line overlay — elegant serif on warm interiors or plain sans on dark garments — over a single product hero; directly portable to Wibes covers built from twin packshots. (2) Multi-product roundups live on warm cream canvases with editorial-serif headlines and numbered circle badges, which is the perfect vehicle for NORVIA's identical-geometry colorway lineups on Pinterest. (3) A consistent styling law worth baking into on-model twin prompts: light puffer worn open over an all-black inner column, or black puffer anchoring exactly one loud piece — always shot on seamless light-grey/cream, often with a mid-motion pose.

This batch splits cleanly into two tiers: 9 of 14 are text-free street-style singles whose value is styling formulas (monochrome chocolate total-look, one-accent-color rule, hoodie-under-coat, single color pop on neutral scene) that should be encoded as scene/outfit prompts for twin lifestyle renders, not copied as layouts. The four A-grade layouts share one repeating device worth hard-coding into generation: a dedicated text zone (top plate or headline strip) with a numbered/benefit RU promise, over garment-first imagery — and the two most NORVIA-native formats are the side-by-side colorway A/B comparison (our identical-geometry twins do this better than any human creator) and white WB-артикул captions floated next to items for instant shoppability. Palette law across everything: neutral earth monochromes (chocolate, beige, olive, black) with exactly one accent color or one shine texture.

The dominant repeating pattern is the 9:16 'clean wall + full-body model + one short text element' reel cover: neutral interior or wall, jacket-led outfit centered, and either a serif/sans two-tier headline top-center ('PUFFER JACKET / outfit ideas'), a white pill plate lower-third ('The Trench: 5 Ways'), or a native serialization label ('look 1') — all three text devices should be encoded as standard caption components for twin-based Wibes generation. Second pattern: tonal/monochrome color logic (beige puffer on beige street, white puffer with cream pants, black+one-accent) — generation prompts should force bottoms and backdrop to echo or deliberately offset the twin's colorway rather than randomize. Third, the highest-save static formats are 'formula' constructions — palette-dot rail + flat-lay outfit, and the folded colorway stack — both trivially reproducible from identical-geometry twins and directly usable as Pinterest pins and WB card slides.

The dominant winning pattern in this batch is garment-as-living-object art direction — levitation off a ledge (Nike), invisible-person outfit assembly (Spartoo), sculptural folded garment (Love Republic STUDIO) — which turns a model-free packshot into a scroll-stopper and is perfectly suited to our front-view twins; encode 'levitate/pose/fold the twin on a color field sampled from its own colorway' as a generation prompt family. Second pattern: text is either absent or a single device (one corner wordmark, one center pill, one top outlined caption) — image-maximal, text-minimal, so our infographic layer should cap at one text element per frame. Third: emotion/series repetition (same pose, same wink, colorway swapped) builds collectible-set recognition that our identical-geometry color lineups can replicate mechanically.

The A-tier of this batch is unanimous: textless full-bleed street-style singles where ONE styling idea does all the work — luxe accessorization of a black puffer, an RU-native snowy brick street behind a pastel blanket coat, or a saturated contrast underlayer beneath an open grey coat. These are direct prompt recipes for dressing NORVIA twins into scenes (backdrop + 3 accessories + one color rule), no infographic layer needed. Second pattern: size guides are a save-magnet but every strong one couples the table with measurement arrows drawn ON the garment — since our twins share identical geometry, one annotated A/B/C/D template can be stamped across the entire lineup as a standard WB card slide. Third, for video the winning hook frames are either product-held-to-camera with a single caption pill or a thin-serif title floating in empty top space over a mirror-check/walking loop — both are one-line text devices our generation pipeline can template.

This batch is 12/14 single-look puffer street style, and the winning pattern is remarkably consistent: full-body vertical (2:3–4:5), tonal neutral outfit where the puffer is the only volume statement, muted urban or blank-wall backdrop, zero text, plus either one accent color (neon beanie) or a strict monochrome total look — encode "full-body, blank/urban backdrop, tonal styling from the lineup palette, look-down or walking pose" directly into twin lifestyle-render prompts. Two format-level steals rise above the rest: the MULVAN colorway-inversion diptych (a perfect structural match for identical-geometry twin lineups, usable on WB cards, Pinterest and Wibes split-screens) and the white-plate typewriter-font "X Puffer Coat Outfit Ideas" video-cover formula for Wibes, replicable per colorway. Text belongs only on video covers; all static pins in this niche win by being clean and text-free.

Three mechanics dominate this batch: (1) full-bleed vertical hero garment with ONE centered typographic hook — meme-serif POV caption, serif+script lockup, or a giant single-word WB headline — text is always centered over the garment, never tucked in a corner; (2) colorway-as-hero storytelling: monochrome total looks and rare pastel colorways in golden light, plus full-body+detail-crop diptychs — a perfect match for our identical-geometry twin lineups; (3) a shoppability layer (артикул captions under cutouts, numeric pills, torn size badges) that converts any pretty image into a buyable card. Generation prompts should default to: centered 1-3-word RU headline + one badge device (size/temp/артикул) + colorway-monochrome styling, with the jacket as the final reveal in video builds.

Strongest repeating pattern: артикул-as-a-layer — the winning references burn shoppability text straight into the image (LOVE REPUBLIC's 'Арт:' captions per element, plain white 'Артикул:' on UGC try-ons, CapsulesWB's watermark-gap loop), so generation prompts should always reserve a typography slot for артикул rather than leaving it to captions. Second pattern: abundance-of-choice hooks — stacks of folded colors, rack flip-throughs, haul boxes — which map one-to-one onto NORVIA's identical-geometry color lineups and should become our default Wibes openers. Third: the premium band template (packshot on light-gray field + white text band with product-type headline + артикул right-aligned) is the cleanest brand-grade pin format and is trivially reproducible from front-view twins.

The batch splits into two systematic, highly automatable formulas: (1) the WB-card plate system — full-bleed model/street photo kept clean in the center while corners and a left rail carry rounded plates in a fixed hierarchy (category word at billboard scale → temp range with thermometer icon → size range → color dots/fabric icon), with hard numbers (300 г/м², -30°C, 42-60) acting as the trust layer; (2) the curator артикул-formula — 2x2 crop grid or single hero with 'КАТЕГОРИЯ' caps + white rounded pill 'Арт ВБ ######' at the center seam, identical across every product. Encode both as rigid templates over NORVIA twins: the plate hierarchy for slide 1, the quadrant benefit-pill grid for slide 2, spec panels for slide 3, and артикул pills for Pinterest; note the tone fork — bold black grotesque = mass/trend coding, serif + gold-on-dark = premium coding — so palette/typography should be a template parameter, not a fixed choice.

This batch splits cleanly into two production families NORVIA should encode: (1) a master infographic template — giant category headline dyed to the garment color, size-range pill top-left, icon benefit plate, circular fabric-macro badge, color-swatch checkmark pills — reused verbatim across color-twin артикулы (the two AM&PA slides prove sellers literally recolor one template per colorway, which maps 1:1 onto our identical-geometry twin lineups). (2) Text-free editorial slides where a single feature sells photographically: hood-up close crops, monochrome total looks, and scenic composites (glacier, night city) that inflate perceived value. The minimum viable text layer across winners is just a size-range numeral block in the top-left corner — big numbers (sizes, temperature ranges) consistently outperform adjective copy.

This batch is a dense WB-card masterclass with one dominant law: temperature range is the category's universal numeric hook — 'до -30/-35°C' or '+10/-10°' appears on nearly every text-bearing slide, always oversized or badge-framed, and should be a mandatory field in NORVIA's infographic layer. Second pattern: a single giant trend/season word ('ТРЕНД', 'ОСЕНЬ', 'ТРЕНД СЕЗОНА', 'КОЛЛЕКЦИЯ 2026') in display type carries the fashion claim, while sizes live in a small corner pill — never more than 3-4 info blocks per slide. Third and most twin-compatible: the dark cinematic ghost-mannequin hero (SmileStyle) is a fixed-coordinate template re-skinned per colorway — the exact economics of NORVIA's identical-geometry color lineups — and zero-text macro/lifestyle slides mark the premium tier, so text density should decrease as price increases.

Strongest repeating pattern: the SmileStyle ghost-mannequin hero run twice in different colorways proves the winning move is one locked cinematic template (floating garment, tone-matched gradient background, spotlight floor) parameterized per color — exactly what our twin color-lineups are built for. Nearly every A-grade card carries the same info triad — size range (42-60), temp promise (до -30/-35°С), and one giant trend/category word — so this triad should be a mandatory layer in generation prompts, with plates for budget lines and plateless tone-matched type for dark/premium colorways. Third law: infographic density scales inversely with price — budget ветровки get icon-bullet benefit panels and pills, premium пуховики get clean packshots plus textless macro detail slides (croppable from existing twin renders at zero cost).

Strongest repeating pattern: one full-bleed model/twin shot plus a single high-contrast text plate carrying exactly one message — a category headline, an objection-killer claim, a verdict label, or a runway-credit nameplate — never more than one idea per frame; encode "1 frame = 1 claim on 1 plate" into generation prompts. Second pattern: assortment/choice displays (fanned hanger hauls, colorway walls, устарело/база/модно triptychs) map perfectly onto NORVIA's identical-geometry color lineups and should become a first-class template family. Third: color-pop staging — a saturated garment as the only chromatic object against beige stone/grey concrete/white tile — is the cheapest reliable scroll-stopper and works identically for packshots, pins, and i2v motion clips.

items.layout: Single full-bleed vertical frame, model centered against flat white wall with natural hard light; candid head-tilt pose, hands on hips flaring the oversized shirt silhouette; 100% image, no text zones.
